title: Hark! Hark! with Harps of Gold
description: Hark! Hark! with Harps of Gold in Tonic Solfa to DIADEMATA, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Edwin Hubbell Chapin wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 203 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “The Same”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Short Metre Double (6.6.8.6.6.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to DIADEMATA; any other Short Metre Double tune fits them as well.
underlay: Hark! hark! with harps of gold, What an-them do they sing? The ra-diant clouds have back-ward_ rolled, And an-gels smite the string. "Glo-ry to God!" bright wings Spread glist'n-ing and a-far, And on the hal-lowed rap-ture rings From cir-cling star to star.

lines: Hark! hark! with harps of gold,
The radiant clouds have backward rolled,
And on the hallowed rapture rings
The glad earth and the sea;
And every wind and billow fleet,
Each holy spot has found a tongue;
And every seraph bends his brow
And fall like dew-drops to the earth?
Soft! — yet the soul is bound
Sound, harps, and hail the morn
For unto us this day is born

licence: Public domain: Edwin Hubbell Chapin died in 1880.
credits: Words by Edwin Hubbell Chapin (1814–1880), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to DIADEMATA by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
